insights.title: United Kingdom leads the market
insights.body: 85.5% of gross merchandise sales come from this market in the selected period.

insights.title: A concentrated product portfolio
insights.body: The top 20% of products generate 78.6% of gross merchandise sales. Use the Pareto curve to explore the long tail.

insights.title: Customer identity has gaps
insights.body: 13.1% of gross sales have no customer ID. Sales remain included; customer analyses use identified shoppers only.

methods.clustering: K-means (k up to 4), seeded at 42 with 10 initializations; standardized log1p recency, frequency and monetary value. Silhouette uses at most 1,500 sampled customers. Cluster numbers ranked by average spend, not by inherent quality.
methods.basket: Two-item Apriori: top 80 products by distinct sale-invoice frequency; each product appears once per basket. Minimum count max(20, ceil(0.2% of baskets)), confidence ≥15%, lift >1. Supports use all selected positive merchandise invoices. Top 20 directional rules by lift; associations are not causation.
methods.cohort: First observed purchase within the selected date and country scope; not proven lifetime acquisition. Cohort age is calendar months. Unobserved future months are null. Current partial month can understate retention.
methods.scope: Exact duplicates removed. Merchandise stock codes only (five digits with up to two trailing letters); service, postage and manual adjustment codes excluded. Positive prices and nonzero quantities required. C-prefixed invoices treated as negative credits. Missing customer IDs retained for sales, excluded from customer analysis. Net revenue = positive merchandise sales less observed credits/negative quantities; credits may refer to sales outside the selected period. AOV uses positive sales / distinct positive invoices. No cost or profit data.
